title: Microbatch quant research scrap — Oct 29 2027
content:
Quick context:
- Short capture after this week’s microbatch experiments. Goal: understand interactions between microbatch sizes, q4_k_m vs q4_0 behavior, and KV-cache pressure on long-context retention during model onboarding tests.
- Meeting cadence: informal 30m sync + short hands-on bench time; notes below are raw.

Attendees / who did what:
- Maya Chen (owner for this doc) — ran the main microbatch sweep, compiled results
- Arjun Patel — adjusted batching pipeline and wrote the runner harness for mixed-precision runs
- Sofia Morales — ran evals (instruction-following, MRR on rerank tasks) and sanity checks
- Luca Bianchi — investigated memory traces and KV eviction patterns on A100 80GB

Experiment snapshot (runner config):
- Model: open-llm/redwood-v1-like (placeholder) small variant used for fast sweeps
- Sequences: variable (avg user seq ~230 tokens, tail ~1.2k tokens)
- Microbatch sizes tested: 1, 2, 4, 8
- Batching windows: 5ms, 10ms, 25ms
- Quant formats: q4_0, q4_k_m (and a single run q8_0 as sanity)
- KV cache policy: LRU eviction at 76% mem threshold (controlled in runtime)
- HW: A100-80GB + one A10 for cross-check

Quick plain-English findings (high-level):
- Latency vs throughput: microbatch=1 gives best P99 at small load but terrible throughput. microbatch=4 with 10ms window hits the best steady-state tradeoff for our synthetic tail workload.
- q4_k_m consistently reduced memory used but showed a tiny regression in instruction-following BLEU-like heuristics (~0.6-1.4% relative) versus q4_0.
- Under heavy long-context cases (>=1024 tokens), KV eviction triggered more with microbatch>4 because the runtime coalesced requests into larger in-memory KV frames; leads to observable hallucination-rate increase in a small subset (~2% of prompts).
- q8_0 run was stable (no instruction drop) but increased tail latency by ~12% and doubled memory pressure. Not viable for most Hosted targets but fine for Dedicated profiles.

Mini metrics table (aggregated across 3 runs each):
- Metric definitions: P50/P95/P99 generation latency (ms), tokens/sec (throughput), Inst-Foll (instruction-following score, 0-100), MRR@10 (rerank), mem-peak (GB)

Config | P99 (ms) | tok/s | Inst-Foll | MRR@10 | mem-peak
micro1-q4_0 | 230 | 4.5 | 87.6 | 0.72 | 21.1
micro4-q4_0 | 410 | 12.8 | 86.9 | 0.71 | 23.5
micro4-q4_k_m | 395 | 13.0 | 86.0 | 0.70 | 18.8
micro8-q4_k_m | 540 | 18.2 | 85.4 | 0.69 | 19.2
micro4-q8_0 | 460 | 11.2 | 88.4 | 0.73 | 39.6

Observations / weird behavior:
- There is a pattern where q4_k_m runs, when combined with microbatch>=4, show a small but consistent drop on a narrow set of instruction-paraphrase pairs (Sofia's eval set id eval-instr-v2). Hypothesis: quant noise interacts with batching order and local KV precision leading to brittle decoding in low-probability branches.
- Luca found intermittent KV chunk recomputation spikes in traces at the point when many long-context requests arrive concurrently; this spikes GC-like cleanup and forces eviction earlier than the memory threshold suggests (looks like fragmentation).
- We saw one reproducible case where the second half of a multi-turn dialogue lost entity consistency after an eviction event. Repro steps: use seq lengths 1k and 300, back-to-back, microbatch=8, q4_k_m.

Actionable hypotheses to test next week:
1) Add per-request KV pinning flag to keep first N=3 requests' KV segments resident for short time to avoid immediate eviction in bursty tails. (owner: Luca, due: 2027-11-05)
2) Run targeted evals on eval-instr-v2 with stratified prompting (low vs high branching) to quantify where quant+batching hurts. (owner: Sofia, due: 2027-11-03)
3) Microbenchmark varying batching-window vs batching-count independently (we currently couple them); measure P99 and mem-peak. (owner: Arjun, due: 2027-11-04)
4) Try stochastic rounding variant of q4_k_m (experimental) and a middle ground q6-lite to see if instruction-drop recovers. (owner: Maya, due: 2027-11-09)

Onboarding checklist updates (notes for model onboarding doc):
- Add a microbatch stress-test step to onboarding checklist: "simulate tail bursts with mixed seq lengths" (confluence: CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-6789#microbatch-test).
- Record per-model recommended default microbatch and quant profile (field: suggested-runtime-presets).
- Include a short note on KV pin lifetime tradeoffs and an example config snippet for private customers.

Open questions / blockers:
- Is the observed hallucination increase strictly due to numeric quant noise or a systemic batching + eviction interplay? Need an ablation that isolates eviction without quant changes.
- If we pin KV segments to avoid eviction, what is the cost model for Hosted? Add rough estimate to ticket JIRA-INF-2214 for product.
- Are there edge-case prompt formats that amplify the quant effect (e.g., certain tokenization patterns)? Sofia to run tokenizer-entropy check across failing prompts.

Notes from short sync (2027-10-29):
- Decided to prioritize a non-invasive runtime flag for KV pinning (fast path) so we can A/B on Dedicated customers first.
- Agreement to add a short eval harness that runs during onboarding (10-15 minutes) that simulates 200 mixed-seq requests to observe mem-peak and P99.

Stash / ephemeral artifacts:
- Runner script: github PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/rundown/pull/452 (bench harness for microbatch sweep)
- Eval bucket: s3://redwood-evals/eval-instr-v2/oct29-2027 (Sofia)
- Trace capture: gs://redwood-traces/applied-ml/microbatch-oct29/trace-001 (Luca)

Immediate next steps (short list):
- Arjun: decouple batching window vs count; push harness changes and post results in #applied-ml (slack link in linked_artifacts).
- Sofia: run stratified evals, post failing prompts + tokenization quirks as gist under PR.
- Luca: prototype KV pin flag in runtime locally and run with micro4/q4_k_m to see if eviction episodes go away.
- Maya: spin up q6-lite conversion script and run small eval set; coordinate with product on Dedicated trial note.

Misc notes / random thoughts (brainstorm):
- Could we expose a "burst protection" policy at the API layer that temporarily reduces batching for a customer's requests if we detect long-context bursts?
- Consider a quant-aware reranker that runs in float32 on a small shortlist to correct rare instruction drops (cost tradeoff: small increase in tokens but maybe significant quality recovery).

End of scrap. Will convert into a cleaned onboarding checklist + a tidy post next week if results converge.

Links referenced:
- JIRA: INF-2214 (cost model + runtime flag request)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PLATFORM-6789 (microbatch onboarding section)
